summary: Two Chinese-linked supertankers have U-turned in the Strait of Hormuz as risks to shipping remain elevated, with prospects for a normalization of traffic dimming after President Donald Trump took a hard line on Iran.

title: Hitachi Construction Shares Drop After $740 Million Block Trades
summary: Hitachi Construction Machinery Co.’s shares fell the most in almost three weeks after its major shareholder Hitachi Ltd. offloaded all its holdings, in the latest move by the Japanese conglomerate to divest some of its assets to focus on core businesses.

title: Carry Traders Pivot to Swiss Franc After Yen Volatility Spikes
summary: Carry traders are increasingly turning to the Swiss franc in the near term for their source of funding as the threat of intervention and higher interest rates saps the appeal of borrowing in the yen.

title: Chip Stocks Sell Off, Government Bonds Edge Higher: Markets Wrap

title: Fesharaki: US in 'Strong Position' to Wait Out Iran
summary: FGE NexantECA Chairman Emeritus Fereidun Fesharaki tells Bloomberg TV that Iran can only survive a few more months of curtailed income due to the Strait of Hormuz conflict. He adds that the US may consider waiting out the regime for a better deal. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Pimco’s Stracke Says Wealth Firms Running Shy of Private Credit
summary: Wealth managers are beating a retreat from private credit and ramping up a search for alternatives, as they continue to reel from sudden exit restrictions at several major direct lending funds earlier this year.

title: Fesharaki: Oil’s Real Story Lies in Products, Not Crude
summary: FGE NexantECA Chairman Emeritus Fereidun Fesharaki argues that the refined oil product markets have decoupled from crude oil, reshaping how we understand global energy dynamics. He stresses that to truly grasp the direction of oil markets, we must watch gasoline, diesel and jet fuel trends more closely than crude benchmarks. He speaks with Haslinda Amin on "Insight with Haslinda Amin. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Chinese Cartoon So Bad You Have to See It Becomes Box Office Hit
summary: A low-budget cartoon about a calf has become an unlikely box-office sensation in China, turning online ridicule into millions of dollars in ticket sales and sparking a debate over the merits of crude animation in the age of polished AI-generated entertainment.

title: CXMT Rival YMTC Moves Closer to China’s Next Marquee Chip IPO

title: AiMoGA Sees Auto-Robot Integration as Key to Growth
